analysis.title: PNC Weekly Market Watch: Rocky rotation redux (October 26, 2026)
key_insights: Global equities mostly fell last week. On October 22 the S&P 500 posted its largest one-day decline in more than two months, after Meta Platforms' recapitalization plan announcement raised concerns about the sustainability of AI financing.

Information Technology and growth stocks fell the most, in the US and abroad. The Russell 3000 Value ended the week positive and had its best weekly outperformance over Russell 3000 Growth in more than two years, as investors rotated away from mega-cap stocks.

The 10-year UST yield fell 17 bps on October 22, its biggest one-day drop since August 2024, as investors questioned whether AI-supported economic growth could be sustained. It ended the week near 5.0%, below the early October peak of 5.3%.
Brent crude rose to a five-month high of nearly $116 per barrel after attacks on infrastructure in Saudi Arabia.

The FOMC meets this week. Markets expect no change in policy, with a high probability of a rate hike in December. Post-meeting messaging, higher bond yields, geopolitical uncertainty and the US midterm elections could add to volatility.
PNC maintains its lean toward diversified equities.

With 25% of S&P 500 constituents reported, blended earnings growth is 29.5%, up 50 bps from the prior week. Early Mag 7 results were positive, but investor concerns about the capex needed to support AI growth weighed heavily on most of the group's share prices.

Weekly performance as of 10/23: S&P 500 -0.5%, Growth -1.8%, Value +1.1%, Russell 2000 +2.0%, MSCI World ex USA -1.4%, MSCI EM IMI -2.8%. Gold fell 4.1% to $3,996/oz and crude oil rose 4.4% to $103.27/barrel.

Valuations: S&P 500 trades at 18.6x P/E vs a 3-year average of 20.9x. Growth is at 19.6x vs 25.7x, Value at 17.5x vs 17.2x. The S&P 500 (7,624) is below its 50-day average (7,700) and above its 200-day (7,291).
Fixed income: Bloomberg US Corp HY OAS is 337 bps vs a 3-year median of 292 bps. US Corp IG OAS is 89 bps vs 82 bps. EM USD Agg OAS is 191 bps vs 215 bps.
earnings_insights: S&P 500 Q3 2026 blended earnings growth is 29.5% (actual results plus consensus for companies yet to report) vs a 9/30/26 estimate of 29.2%, a 0.3 pt surprise, with 24.5% of companies reported as of 10/23.
S&P 500 ex-Mag 7 blended growth is 29.6% vs a 27.9% estimate, a 1.7 pt surprise, with 24.4% reported.

Sector blended growth vs 9/30/26 estimate: Communication Services 39.8% vs 51.5% (-11.7 pts), Energy 136.0% vs 114.8% (+21.3 pts), Information Technology 65.6% vs 63.8% (+1.8 pts), Health Care -1.2% vs 5.6% (-6.8 pts), Industrials 17.6% vs 14.6% (+2.9 pts), Financials 4.6% vs 3.0% (+1.6 pts).
Reporting progress by sector: Financials 47.4%, Consumer Discretionary 31.9%, Industrials 30.1%, Info Tech 16.2%, Health Care 13.3%, Utilities 6.5%.
